newsitem.title: USA: Florida immigration lawsuit to be filed Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Florida immigration lawsuit to be filed Wednesday.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles will sue the federal government on Wednesday over state costs associated with the cutoff of benefits to legal immigrants, Chiles' press office said.
The governor scheduled a news conference Wednesday at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT in Tallahassee to discuss the suit. It was unclear whehter it would be filed in U.S. District Court in Tallahassee or Miami.
While Florida and other states have sued the federal government previously over immigration-related costs, Florida would become the first to sue over changes enacted in the 1996 welfare reform law.
Chiles said more than 100,000 legal immigrants in Florida would lose food stamps, Supplemental Security Income payments and other benefits that help pay for food and other basic living expenses.
State officials said the changes would cost Florida between $65 million and $1 billion a year and those costs should be borne by the federal government.
